To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the growth of hospital spending in Spain is mainly driven by an increase in the number of hospital admissions and by the growth in the number of beds, while the growth of average length of stay (ALOS) is not statistically significant in the short run, but it has an important role in the long run.

the growth in hospital expenditure in Spain was driven by a significant increase in the number of hospital discharges, a significant increase in hospital discharges with higher complexity and a significant increase in prices.

the growth in hospital spending was largely driven by the increase in the volume of hospital activity and by the increase in prices of hospital services, and that the increase in the prices of hospital services was mainly caused by the increase in labor costs.

the factors underlying the growth of public hospital expenditure in Spain during the last decade (2000–2009).

the Spanish healthcare system is not only a system of high quality and equity, but also a system that is efficient in terms of the resources it uses.

the economic recession in Spain, which started in 2007 and lasted until 2013, has been associated with a reduction of hospital costs in Spain, which has been mainly driven by a decrease in the number of hospital discharges, a reduction in the average length of stay and a decrease in the average cost per discharge.

we have developed an innovative approach for the analysis of hospital expenditure, using a dynamic panel data model.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of the Spanish healthcare system has been mainly explained by the growth of the population, the growth of prices and the increase in the number of procedures performed.
the use of administrative data in the context of a dynamic panel model can provide a more accurate picture of the factors driving hospital expenditure than a static panel model.
, in the Spanish hospital setting, the growth of expenditure is mainly driven by the increase of hospital beds, which in turn is explained by the growth of hospital admissions.
